newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Enlargement to top informal GAC next month.
newsitem.headline: Enlargement to top informal GAC next month.

text.p: Enlargement is expected to top the agenda of the informal European Union foreign ministers meeting in Apeldoorn on March 15 and 16, EU diplomats said on Monday.
The foreign ministers are expected in particular to discuss how to proceed with beginning negotiations with the 10 former communist bloc countries that have been promised eventual EU membership.
"On the EU side, some of the big issues are differentiation or non-differentiation" one diplomat said.

At issue is whether to start negotiations with all the countries -- Poland, Hungary, the Czech republic, Slovakia, Slovenia, Bulgaria, Romania, Estonia, Lithuania and Latvia -- at the same time, or accept that some are not ready for membership.
Officially, the EU has said that it hopes to begin negotiations six months after the end of the inter-governmental conference with those countries deemed ready by the European Commission.
One view has been that negotiations should begin with all the eastern applicants at the same time, but some countries question the wisdom of such a move.
"To formally begin with a wide group of people -- some of whom you know (are not going to make it) -- is bad politics," one EU government official said.
Part of the discussion will also involve the relationship -- if any -- between EU enlargement and that of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation.
The ministers are also expected to discuss the role of Turkey, which is still actively seeking EU membership and which has threatened to block NATO enlargement if it is not satisfied.
While most countries view Turkey as a separate case, Britain argues that it should not be left out in the cold.
"You shouldn't treat them totally separate from the other EU applicants," a British official said.
